arxiv-1311-4799.title: Adaptive Hierarchical Data Aggregation using Compressive Sensing (A-HDACS) for Non-smooth Data Field
arxiv-1311-4799.creator: Xi Xu, Rashid Ansari, Ashfaq Khokhar
arxiv-1311-4799.description: A 2013 arXiv research paper by Xi Xu, Rashid Ansari, Ashfaq Khokhar. Compressive Sensing (CS) has been applied successfully in a wide variety of applications in recent years, including photography, shortwave infrared cameras, optical system research, facial recognition, MRI, etc. In wireless sensor networks (WSNs), significant research work has been pursued to investigate the use of CS to reduce the amount of data communicated, particularly in data aggregation applications and thereby improving energy efficiency.

arxiv-2205-11811.title: Sensing Performance of Multi-Channel RFID-based Finger Augmentation Devices for Tactile Internet
arxiv-2205-11811.creator: F. Naccarata, G. M. Bianco and G. Marrocco
arxiv-2205-11811.description: Abstract Radiofrequency finger augmentation devices (R-FADs) are a recently introduced class of epidermal radiofrequency identification (RFID) sensor-tags attached to the fingers, communicating with a body-worn reader. These devices are promising candidates to enable Tactile Internet (TI) applications in the short term. R-FAD based on auto-tuning RFID microchips can be used as dielectric probes for the material of touched objects.

arxiv-2303-06764.title: Combinatorial proofs of Merca’s identities involving the sum of different parts congruent to r r modulo m m in all partitions of n n
arxiv-2303-06764.creator: Cristina Ballantine
arxiv-2303-06764.description: Abstract . We give combinatorial proofs of several recent results due to Merca on the sum of different parts congruent to r r modulo m m in all partitions of n n . The proofs make use of some well known involutions from the literature and some new involutions introduced here. Keywords: partitions, bijections, involutions, recurrences.

arxiv-2311-06116.creator: Lorenzo Ceragioli, Fabio Gadducci, Giuseppe Lomurno, Gabriele Tedeschi
arxiv-2311-06116.description: Abstract . Past years have seen the development of a few proposals for quantum extensions of process calculi. The rationale is clear: with the development of quantum communication protocols, there is a need to abstract and focus on the basic features of quantum concurrent systems, like CCS and CSP have done for their classical counterparts.

arxiv-2406-10145.title: Reconstruction Plans and Efficient Rank-1 Lattice Construction for Chebyshev Expansions Over Lower Sets Thanks: College of Computing, University Mohammed VI Polytechnic, Morocco. abdelqoddous.moussa@um6p.ma . Thanks: moulay-abdellah.chkifa@polytechnique.org
arxiv-2406-10145.creator: Abdelqoddous Moussa, Moulay Abdellah Chkifa
arxiv-2406-10145.description: Abstract . This study focuses on constructing efficient rank-1 lattices that enable the exact integration and reconstruction of functions within Chebyshev spaces, based on finite lower index sets. We establish the equivalence of different reconstruction plans under specific conditions for certain lower sets.

arxiv-2504-08994.title: ReCA: A Parametric ReLU Composite Activation Function
arxiv-2504-08994.creator: John Chidiac john.chidiac@lau.edu, Danielle Azar danielle.azar@lau.edu.lb
arxiv-2504-08994.description: Abstract Activation functions have been shown to affect the performance of deep neural networks significantly. While the Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU) remains the dominant choice in practice, the optimal activation function for deep neural networks remains an open research question.

arxiv-2504-09926.title: Quotients of Poisson boundaries, entropy, and spectral gap
arxiv-2504-09926.creator: Samuel Dodds, Alex Furman
arxiv-2504-09926.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Samuel Dodds, Alex Furman. Poisson boundary is a measurable Γ \Gamma -space canonically associated with a group Γ \Gamma and a probability measure μ \mu on it. The collection of all measurable Γ \Gamma -equivariant quotients, known as μ \mu -boundaries, of the Poisson boundary forms a partially ordered set, equipped with a strictly monotonic non-negative function, known as Furstenberg or differential entropy.

arxiv-2505-00069.title: Superfluid Weight of Inhomogeneous Superconductors
arxiv-2505-00069.creator: Jonathan Schirmer, Enrico Rossi
arxiv-2505-00069.description: Abstract In this work, we obtain the expression, within the linear response approximation, of the superfluid weight of a superconductor, taking into account the response of the superconductor’s pairing potential to the perturbing vector potential. We find that, in general, the correction is non-zero when the system is spatially non-uniform.

pmc-10478260.title: Prioritizing educational initiatives on emerging technologies for Italian pediatricians: bibliometric review and a survey
pmc-10478260.creator: Alberto Eugenio Tozzi, Francesco Gesualdo, Elisabetta Pandolfi, Diana Ferro, Giulia Cinelli, Elena Bozzola, Tommaso Aversa, Antonio Di Mauro, Chiara Mameli, Ileana Croci
pmc-10478260.description: BackgroundEmerging technologies have demonstrated outstanding potential in improving healthcare, yet their full integration remains a challenge for all medical specialties, including pediatrics. To support the swift implementation of technologies, we identified the current trends through a bibliometric review, and we conducted a survey on Italian pediatricians to gauge educational needs and willingness to integrate technologies into clinical practice.

pmc-11314204.title: Triaxiality and Plastic-Strain-Dependent Proposed PEAK Parameter for Predicting Crack Formation in Polypropylene Polymer Reservoir Subjected to Pressure Load
pmc-11314204.creator: Adam Kasprzak
pmc-11314204.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This article raises the topic of the critical examination of polypropylene, a key polymeric material, and its extensive application within the automotive industry, particularly focusing on the manufacturing of brake fluid reservoirs. This study aims to enhance the understanding of polypropylene’s behavior under mechanical stresses through a series of laboratory destruction tests and numerical simulations, emphasizing the finite element method (FEM).

pmc-11430863.description: PurposeRenal cell carcinoma (RCC) is the most common and lethal type of urogenital cancer, with one-third of new cases presenting as metastatic RCC (mRCC), which, being the seventh most common cancer in men and the ninth in women, poses a significant challenge.

pmc-11593171.title: Association of HLA-G Expression, Its Genetic Variants and Related Neuro-Immunomodulation with Characteristics of Bladder Carcinoma
pmc-11593171.creator: Vladimira Durmanova, Iveta Mikolaskova, Eszter Zsemlye, Agata Ocenasova, Helena Bandzuchova, Magda Suchankova, Boris Kollarik, Patrik Palacka, Milan Zvarik, Maria Bucova, Luba Hunakova
pmc-11593171.description: Simple SummaryHuman leukocyte antigen G (HLA-G) is an immunosuppressive molecule that is often found at higher levels in various cancers, including bladder cancer (BC). We looked at 89 BC patients and 74 control subjects to understand how HLA-G is linked to BC progression.

pmc-12543832.title: Brain Atrophy and Leukoencephalopathy Following Tarlatamab: Case Report
pmc-12543832.creator: Kiriko Onishi, Toki Kitano, Yusuke Fujioka, Moeko Ota, Fumie Onishi, Kohei Miyake, Hisaaki Tanaka, Nobukazu Fujimoto
pmc-12543832.description: We describe the case of a 74‐year‐old female diagnosed with extensive‐stage small cell lung cancer. Initially, she received carboplatin, etoposide and atezolizumab, followed by amrubicin as second‐line treatment and nogitecan as third‐line treatment. Stereotactic radiotherapy was delivered to subsequent brain metastases. Two years after the initial treatment, new brain and lung metastases developed.

pmc-12645097.title: The genome sequence of the Cistus Forester, Adscita geryon (Hübner, [1813]) (Lepidoptera: Zygaenidae)
pmc-12645097.creator: David C. Lees, Natural History Museum Genome Acquisition Lab, Darwin Tree of Life Barcoding Collective, Wellcome Sanger Institute Tree of Life Management, Samples and Laboratory team, Wellcome Sanger Institute Scientific Operations: Sequencing Operations, Wellcome Sanger Institute Tree of Life Core
pmc-12645097.description: We present a genome assembly from an individual female Adscita geryon (Cistus Forester; Arthropoda; Insecta; Lepidoptera; Zygaenidae). The assembly contains two haplotypes with total lengths of 764.63 megabases and 670.15 megabases. Most of haplotype 1 (99.63%) is scaffolded into 32 chromosomal pseudomolecules, including the W and Z sex chromosomes. Haplotype 2 was assembled to scaffold level.

pmc-12694518.title: Deep Learning Meets InSAR for Infrastructure Monitoring: A Systematic Review of Models, Applications, and Challenges
pmc-12694518.creator: Miguel Fontes, Matúš Bakoň, António Cunha, Joaquim J. Sousa
pmc-12694518.description: Monitoring civil infrastructure is increasingly critical due to aging assets, urban expansion, and the need for early detection of structural instabilities. Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) offers high-resolution, all-weather surface deformation monitoring capabilities, which are being enhanced by recent advances in Deep Learning (DL).

pmc-13196581.title: Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation-like bursts in racehorses: do they affect speed and performance? A case control study
pmc-13196581.creator: Fe ter Woort, Guillaume Dubois, Stephen O’Connor, Emmanuelle van Erck-Westergren
pmc-13196581.description: BackgroundParoxysmal atrial fibrillation (pAF) occurs sporadically in horses and has been implicated in poor performance. Diagnosis in large numbers of horses has previously relied on post-exercise ECGs.Hypothesis/ObjectivesDescribe pAF-like bursts detected during exercise and determine their effect on speed, stride, and racing performance.

pmc-13257042.title: The Promise of Synthetic Biology for Redesigning Plant Architecture
pmc-13257042.creator: Suruchi Roychoudhry, Gerard D. dos Santos, James P. B. Lloyd
pmc-13257042.description: Ensuring global food security under accelerating climate change requires transformative approaches to crop improvement that extend beyond the limits of traditional breeding and gene editing. While domestication and modern agriculture have delivered substantial gains in productivity, these advances often came at the cost of genetic diversity, stress resilience, and developmental plasticity.

pmc-13478209.title: A general strategy for access intrinsically antioxidant polyolefins
pmc-13478209.creator: Feiran Yang, Chao Li, Fuzhou Wang, Chen Zou, Changle Chen
pmc-13478209.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The long-term stability of various polyolefins relies on antioxidants. Traditional methods such as physical blending or chemical modification often suffer from non-uniform dispersion, migration, or lack of universality, especially for ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene (UHMWPE). Developing a general strategy to access various polyethylene types bearing intrinsically antioxidant properties (defined as polyolefins with antioxidant properties produced via polymerization, without postpolymerization antioxidant addition) remains a challenge.
